title: The ticket you cannot afford to skip: inside Spain's Christmas lottery

sents.en: Every December, millions of Spaniards buy into the same few numbers, hoping for the prize they call El Gordo, the Fat One.
sents.zh: 每年十二月，数百万西班牙人都会合买同样的几个号码，盼着中那个被他们叫作 El Gordo（“胖子”）的头奖。

sents.en: Few expect to win; what they really fear is being left out.
sents.zh: 没几个人真指望中奖；他们真正怕的，是被落下。

sents.en: The draw, held each year on 22 December, dates back more than two centuries and is broadcast live for hours.
sents.zh: 开奖每年 12 月 22 日举行，历史可以追溯到两百多年前，电视会连续直播好几个小时。

sents.en: Children from a Madrid school sing out the winning numbers and prizes in a distinctive chant that Spaniards recognise instantly.
sents.zh: 来自马德里一所学校的孩子们，用一种独特的吟唱声唱出中奖号码和奖金，西班牙人一听就能认出来。

sents.en: Full tickets are expensive, so most people buy a fraction of one, known as a décimo, a tenth.
sents.zh: 一整张彩票很贵，所以大多数人只买其中一小份，叫作 décimo，也就是十分之一。

sents.en: Many go further and split tickets with colleagues, neighbours, the local bar or the football club.
sents.zh: 很多人更进一步，和同事、邻居、街角酒吧或足球俱乐部一起分摊彩票。

sents.en: This habit of clubbing together is the heart of the tradition.
sents.zh: 这种凑钱合买的习惯，才是这个传统的核心。

sents.en: If an office shares a number and it comes up, half the staff may resign the next morning.
sents.zh: 如果一个办公室合买了一个号码而它中了，第二天早上可能有一半员工辞职。

sents.en: If it comes up and you did not chip in, you may spend years being reminded of it.
sents.zh: 要是号码中了而你没掏钱，你可能会被人念叨好多年。

sents.en: In 2011 the top prize fell on a single village in Aragon, where almost every household had bought a share of the same number.
sents.zh: 2011 年，头奖落在了阿拉贡的一个小村子里，那里几乎家家户户都合买了同一个号码。

sents.en: One man, it is said, had not; the cameras found him, cheerful but rueful, among his newly rich neighbours.
sents.zh: 据说只有一个人没买；镜头找到了他，他站在一夜暴富的邻居中间，开朗中带着几分懊悔。

sents.en: The odds of winning the top prize are slim, roughly one in 100,000 per number.
sents.zh: 中头奖的几率很小，每个号码大约十万分之一。

sents.en: But the lottery spreads its money widely, paying out thousands of smaller prizes, and even a refund for tickets ending in the same digit as the top prize.
sents.zh: 不过这种彩票把钱分得很散：发放成千上万个小奖，尾号和头奖相同的彩票甚至可以退还本钱。

sents.en: Economists grumble that it is a tax on hope.
sents.zh: 经济学家抱怨说，这是一种“希望税”。

sents.en: Yet few Spaniards seem to mind: for many, the ticket is less a bet than a ritual, like a card sent to an old friend.
sents.zh: 可西班牙人似乎并不在意：对很多人来说，这张彩票与其说是赌注，不如说是一种仪式，就像寄给老朋友的一张贺卡。

sents.en: No sooner has the last prize been sung than winners in lucky towns are spraying each other with sparkling wine on national television.
sents.zh: 最后一个奖刚唱完，幸运小镇里的中奖者就已经在全国电视直播中互相喷起起泡酒来了。

sents.en: Shops that sold the winning number hang banners boasting of their luck, and the queues outside them grow longer the following year.
sents.zh: 卖出中奖号码的彩票店会挂出横幅炫耀自己的好运，第二年店门外的队伍也会排得更长。

sents.en: Superstition plays its part, too.
sents.zh: 迷信也起了作用。

sents.en: People travel across the country to buy from outlets with a lucky reputation, and some rub their tickets on a pregnant friend's belly for luck.
sents.zh: 人们跨越大半个国家，去有“幸运”名声的彩票点买票，有的人还会把彩票在怀孕朋友的肚子上蹭一蹭，图个好运。

sents.en: For all the talk of jackpots, the real prize may be the feeling of being in it together.
sents.zh: 尽管大家嘴上都在谈大奖，真正的奖品也许是“大家一起”的那种感觉。

sents.en: In a year of rising prices, a shared ticket is a small, cheap promise that nobody will be forgotten.
sents.zh: 在物价上涨的一年里，一张合买的彩票是一个小小的、便宜的承诺：谁也不会被忘记。

sents.en: Most will lose, of course.
sents.zh: 当然，大多数人都会输。

sents.en: But they will lose together, and that, Spaniards insist, is half the fun.
sents.zh: 但他们会一起输，而西班牙人坚持说，这正是一半的乐趣所在。
